topic: What trade-offs exist between subcarrier interval sizing for CFO robustness and frequency planning in multi-beam architectures?
consensus_response: The subcarrier interval (δf) affects the carrier frequency offset (CFO), dictating minimum δfmin = 2fdmax. For high-speed mobility scenarios, fdmax = 560 Hz. Increasing δf reduces interference but may compromise CFO resilience, while smaller intervals improve CFO robustness at the cost of increased interference risk. Pilot Symbol Assisted Modulation (PSAM) can mitigate CFO effects but increases pilot symbol overhead. Advanced channel estimation methods, such as Least Squares (LS) or Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE), can be used to further mitigate CFO effects when combined with PSAM.
reference_context: The maximum value of the Doppler shift fdmax = 560 Hz dictates the minimum subcarrier interval δfmin = 2fdmax. A suitable subcarrier interval δfra can be chosen based on fdmax and δf to eliminate the influence of CFO in preamble design rather than timing detection.
